summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of frequent hospitalizations for nausea, vomiting, and back pain was admitted with diabetic ketoacidosis due to uncontrolled hyperglycemia. She presented with high blood glucose of 595, an elevated anion gap, and dehydration. She was treated with IV fluids and insulin, which resolved the acidosis. Her diet was advanced successfully, and her blood sugars stabilized. Imaging showed no acute abdominal process. Her insulin regimen was adjusted to 24 units of glargine at bedtime with a revised sliding scale. Acute kidney injury improved with hydration, and lisinopril was restarted. Social work facilitated outpatient mental health and medical follow-up to address ongoing challenges with adherence and anxiety. She was discharged home in stable condition with updated medications and coordinated follow-up care.
